subject.title: fix(process): bound Windows exec timeout cleanup

question: Should Windows foreground exec settlement remain bounded at three seconds when taskkill never completes, accepting best-effort descendant cleanup in that exceptional path?
rationale: The implementation is correct and strongly proven for normal and observed failure paths, but the availability-versus-guaranteed-cleanup tradeoff is intentional runtime policy that a process owner should accept.

options.title: Accept bounded settlement
options.body: Merge the current head so foreground exec cannot hang indefinitely when Windows taskkill itself stalls.

options.title: Require confirmed cleanup
options.body: Pause and redesign the Windows tree-kill contract if descendants must be confirmed terminated before any caller settlement.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded settlement
recommendation.body: Merge the current head so foreground exec cannot hang indefinitely when Windows taskkill itself stalls.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current process-tree/taskkill implementation and merged the related supervisor lifecycle change.
